issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal subclasses: the template Main (and the problem instructions/examples) show instantiation using single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")), while the solution implements Animal and all concrete animals with two-parameter constructors (String name, int age). This prevents students who follow the provided Main examples or the UML (which implies only name) from compiling and confuses the intended constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent with the problem/template examples. Either: (A) Change the solution to use single-parameter constructors (String name) for Animal and its subclasses (remove the extra age parameter and related getters/setters), or (B) Update the problem statement and template Main examples to document and use two-parameter constructors (String name, int age). Prefer option A to match the UML and the provided Main usage.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch for Animal: the UML and problem description indicate Animal has a single attribute name (String) and students are instructed to implement getters/setters for it. The solution adds an extra attribute 'age' with associated getters/setters. This extra attribute is not mentioned in the problem statement and can confuse students about required fields and constructor responsibilities.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Animal class with the problem specification: remove the unexpected 'age' attribute from the solution (and its getters/setters), keeping only the 'name' attribute and its accessor methods; or, if 'age' should be part of the exercise, update the problem statement and UML to document the additional attribute and include it in constructor and example usages in the template.

issues.description: Constructor/signature mismatch for Animal subclasses: the problem statement and the template Main() show and expect single-argument constructors that initialize an animal's name (the UML and examples use only the 'name' attribute), but the solution introduces an additional 'age' attribute on Animal and changes all animal constructors to require (String name, int age). This breaks the direct mapping between the problem/template examples and the solution API and will confuse students (e.g., template Main calls new Seal("Clarabelle") while solution requires new Seal("Clarabelle", age)).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor API across artifacts. Either (A) remove the extra 'age' attribute from the solution and use single-argument constructors Animal(String name) / Seal(String name) / Pig(String name) / Goat(String name) to match the UML/template and examples, or (B) keep 'age' but update the template/problem statement to require and demonstrate two-argument constructors, or (C) provide overloaded constructors in the solution that accept only (String name) in addition to the (String name, int age) constructor so template examples work unchanged.
